screening_decisions.reason: This is an observational study examining the association between alpha-thalassemia co-inheritance and clinical outcomes in SCD patients. It does not evaluate RBC transfusion interventions or compare transfusion strategies. The study focuses on genetic factors affecting disease severity rather than transfusion therapy.

This RCT evaluates hydroxycarbamide (hydroxyurea) versus placebo in young children with SCA. While it mentions reduced transfusions as a secondary outcome, the primary intervention is pharmacological (hydroxycarbamide), not RBC transfusion. The study does not compare transfusion strategies or evaluate transfusion effectiveness directly.

This is a review article discussing iron overload mechanisms and management in transfused SCD patients. While it relates to transfusion consequences, it is not a primary study evaluating transfusion interventions or comparing transfusion strategies. Review articles are typically excluded from systematic reviews of primary studies.

This is a general review article about advances in SCD understanding and therapies. It does not specifically evaluate RBC transfusion interventions or compare transfusion strategies. The scope is too broad and does not address the specific research question.
This is a methodological paper about conducting overviews of systematic reviews. It has no relevance to SCD or RBC transfusion interventions. This is clearly outside the scope of the review.

This RCT directly compares regular blood transfusion therapy versus standard care (observation) for preventing recurrent cerebral infarcts in children with SCD and silent cerebral infarcts. It addresses the core research question of transfusion versus no transfusion for preventing complications (stroke). The study provides high-quality evidence on transfusion effectiveness for stroke prevention.

This RCT compares prophylactic transfusions versus transfusions only for medical/obstetric emergencies in pregnant women with SCD. It directly addresses the research question by comparing two transfusion strategies (prophylactic vs. as-needed) and evaluates both maternal and perinatal outcomes. This is highly relevant to the review objective.

This RCT compares preoperative transfusion versus no preoperative transfusion in SCD patients undergoing surgery. It directly addresses the research question of transfusion versus no transfusion for preventing perioperative complications. The study provides important evidence on the effectiveness of preoperative transfusion strategies.

This is a feasibility study focused on validating sPLA2 as a biomarker for predicting acute chest syndrome. While it mentions transfusion as a potential preemptive treatment, the primary aim is biomarker validation, not evaluating transfusion effectiveness. Only 10 patients were randomized to transfusion vs observation, making this unsuitable for evaluating transfusion interventions.

This is a commentary/review article about SCD management challenges in developing countries. It does not present primary data on RBC transfusion interventions or compare transfusion strategies. Review/commentary articles are typically excluded from systematic reviews of primary studies.

This is a review article about pathophysiological mechanisms (coagulation and inflammation) in SCD. It does not evaluate RBC transfusion interventions or compare transfusion strategies. The focus is on disease mechanisms rather than therapeutic interventions.
This is a methodological paper about reporting guidelines for systematic reviews. It has no relevance to SCD or RBC transfusion interventions. This is clearly outside the scope of the review.

This is a single case report about a patient with SCD and suspected sleep apnea. While the patient had a history of transfusions, this study does not evaluate transfusion interventions or compare transfusion strategies. Case reports are generally excluded from systematic reviews due to lack of comparative data.

This is a basic science/laboratory study examining blood viscosity in mixtures of sickle and normal red cells. While it has implications for transfusion regimens, it is not a clinical study evaluating transfusion interventions in patients. Basic science studies are typically excluded from clinical systematic reviews.

This is a case series of six patients with cerebrovascular disease and pulmonary hypertension in SCD. It describes associations between hemolytic anemia and cerebrovascular disease but does not evaluate RBC transfusion interventions or compare transfusion strategies. Observational case series without intervention comparison are excluded.

This is an epidemiological study providing global estimates of sickle haemoglobin prevalence. It does not evaluate RBC transfusion interventions or compare transfusion strategies. Population-based epidemiological studies are outside the scope of this clinical intervention review.

This observational study evaluates RBC alloimmunization rates in SCD patients receiving transfusions, including those with antigen-matched donors. While not an interventional trial, it provides important safety data on transfusion complications (alloimmunization) which is relevant to the review's safety outcomes. The study examines transfusion practices and their safety implications.

This RCT evaluates isoxsuprine (a vasodilator) versus placebo for treating leg ulcers in SCD. The intervention is pharmacological, not RBC transfusion. The study does not address transfusion interventions or compare transfusion strategies.

This RCT evaluates RGD peptide matrix (topical treatment) versus placebo for treating leg ulcers in SCD. The intervention is topical therapy, not RBC transfusion. The study does not address transfusion interventions or compare transfusion strategies.

This RCT directly compares chronic transfusion therapy versus hydroxycarbamide for maintaining TCD velocities and preventing stroke in children with SCD. One arm receives standard transfusions (to maintain HbS <30%), making this a direct comparison involving transfusion as an intervention. The study provides important evidence on transfusion effectiveness for stroke prevention and allows assessment of whether alternative therapies can substitute for chronic transfusion.
The intervention studied is Arginine Butyrate for leg ulcers, not RBC transfusion. Does not meet the population/intervention criteria.
Directly compares restrictive (conservative) vs liberal (aggressive) transfusion regimens for preventing perioperative complications in SCD. Matches selection criteria.
Discusses the effectiveness and indications for red cell exchange transfusions in treating acute complications (stroke, acute chest syndrome) in SCD. Relevant to transfusion therapy evaluation.
General review of SCD pathophysiology and management. Mentions transfusions only in passing without evaluating comparative effectiveness or safety.
Broad overview of SCD epidemiology and treatment landscape. Does not focus on or evaluate RBC transfusion interventions.
Focuses on migration patterns and changing epidemiology of SCD. Unrelated to transfusion therapy.
Investigates genetic factors modifying SCD phenotype. Does not involve RBC transfusion interventions or outcomes.
RCT comparing no pre-operative transfusion vs transfusion in SCD patients undergoing surgery. Directly addresses transfusion vs no transfusion for perioperative management.
Landmark RCT evaluating chronic transfusion therapy vs standard care for primary stroke prevention in high-risk children with SCD. Directly matches criteria.
RCT comparing chronic transfusion therapy with chelation vs hydroxyurea for stroke prevention and iron management in SCD. Evaluates transfusion effectiveness and safety.
Observational cohort study evaluating LDH as a biomarker for hemolysis and vasculopathy. Does not assess transfusion interventions.
Review summarizing indications, effectiveness, and safety risks (iron overload, alloimmunization) of RBC transfusion therapy for SCD complications. Relevant to the review objective.
Evaluates a herbal extract (Cajanus cajan) for reducing pain crises and hepatomegaly. Intervention is not RBC transfusion.
Compares surgical decompression vs physical therapy for osteonecrosis. Does not involve RBC transfusion.
Methodological paper developing a quality assessment tool for systematic reviews. Unrelated to SCD or transfusion therapy.
Cross-sectional study assessing HIV transmission risk in transfused vs non-transfused children with SCD. Directly addresses transfusion safety outcomes.
RCT evaluating topical wound care agents for leg ulcers. Does not involve RBC transfusion.
